questions.title: Fosinopril can cause angioedema
questions.question: Which antihypertensive medication can cause the rare side effect of angioedema?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Prazosin, an alpha1-blocker, is not associated with ACE-mediated bradykinin accumulation and does not cause angioedema by this mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. ACE inhibitors such as fosinopril decrease bradykinin degradation as well as reducing angiotensin II formation. The resulting bradykinin accumulation is why ACE inhibitors, unlike other antihypertensive classes, carry a recognised, if rare, risk of angioedema. Prazosin, propranolol and amlodipine act through entirely different mechanisms (alpha1 blockade, beta blockade, calcium channel blockade respectively) that do not raise bradykinin levels.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Propranolol, a beta-blocker, does not affect bradykinin metabolism and is not characteristically associated with angioedema.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Amlodipine, a calcium channel blocker, does not affect bradykinin metabolism and is not characteristically associated with angioedema.

questions.learning_objective: State that fosinopril, an ACE inhibitor, can cause angioedema through bradykinin accumulation, unlike prazosin, propranolol or amlodipine.

questions.title: Lisinopril causes a persistent dry cough
questions.question: A 45-year-old man was started on therapy for hypertension and developed a persistent, dry cough. Which is most likely responsible for this side effect?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nifedipine, a calcium channel blocker, is not associated with ACE-mediated bradykinin accumulation and is not the characteristic cause of a persistent dry cough.
explanations.B: Correct. ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril decrease bradykinin degradation, and the resulting accumulation of bradykinin (and substance P) in the airways produces a persistent, dry, irritant cough in a substantial minority of patients -- the most common manifestation of ACE inhibitor intolerance. This mechanism-specific effect is not shared by nifedipine, losartan or atenolol.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Losartan, an ARB, acts downstream of ACE and does not inhibit bradykinin degradation, so it does not characteristically cause this cough (an advantage of ARBs over ACE inhibitors).
explanations.D: Incorrect. Atenolol, a beta-blocker, does not affect bradykinin metabolism and is not the characteristic cause of a persistent dry cough.

questions.learning_objective: State that lisinopril, an ACE inhibitor, is the most likely cause of a persistent dry cough through bradykinin accumulation, unlike nifedipine, losartan or atenolol.
